subject: maths
title: Statistics
description: Interpreting and presenting data in bar charts, pictograms and tables, including one-step and two-step questions.

objectives.statement: Interpret and present data using bar charts, pictograms and tables.
Solve one-step and two-step questions (for example, 'How many more?' and 'How many fewer?') using information presented in scaled bar charts and pictograms and tables.

items.prompt: In a pictogram, one apple symbol stands for 2 apples. What do 3 symbols stand for?
In a pictogram, one star stands for 5 points. A team has 4 stars. How many points is that?
In a pictogram, one circle stands for 10 books. How many circles are needed to show 35 books?

items.statement: In a pictogram, half a symbol can stand for half the value of a whole symbol.

items.prompt: In a pictogram, one sun symbol stands for 4 sunny days. What do 2 symbols stand for?

items.statement: Every pictogram symbol always stands for exactly 1, no matter what the key says.

items.prompt: In a pictogram, one square stands for 2 goals. Team A has 5 squares and Team B has 3 squares. How many more goals did Team A score?

items.statement: On a bar chart, the taller the bar, the bigger the number it shows.

items.prompt: A bar chart shows 8 children chose cats and 12 chose dogs. How many more chose dogs than cats?
On a bar chart, the scale goes up in steps of 2. A bar reaches halfway between 6 and 8. What is its value?
A bar chart shows favourite colours: red 15, blue 9, green 6. How many children voted in total?
A bar chart shows favourite fruits: apples 10, bananas 14, grapes 7. Which fruit was the most popular?
A bar chart shows 20 children walk to school and 13 come by car. How many fewer come by car?
A table shows laps run: Monday 25, Tuesday 32. How many laps were run altogether?
A table shows Class A read 48 books and Class B read 29 books. How many fewer books did Class B read?

items.statement: In a tally chart, a group of five is drawn as four lines with a fifth line across them.

items.prompt: A tally shows two full groups of five and two extra marks. What number is that?
A table shows ice creams sold: Saturday 30, Sunday 40. On which day were more ice creams sold?
A table shows stickers collected: Amy 24, Ben 18, Cara 30. How many do Amy and Ben have altogether?

items.statement: A table with rows and columns can show the same information as a bar chart.
